newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo offers partnership to Belgian businesses.
newsitem.headline: Yugo offers partnership to Belgian businesses.

text.p: Yugoslavia called on Thursday for more balanced trade with Belgium and offered Belgian businesses partnership and industrial cooperation.

"We offer you partnership and joint ventures in industrial production clearing the way for customs exemption to Belgian firms," head of the Serbian Chamber of Commerce Vlajko Stojiljkovic told his counterpart Jacques Isaac Castiau, president of the Brussels Chamber of Commerce and Industry.
Stojiljkovic said Yugoslavia was interested in high technology and equipment. Castiau said the key to expanding trade was to get more medium and small companies involved.
Yugoslavia used to sell furniture, textiles, frozen fruit, raw magnesium and enamelled kitchen ware to Belgium and bought mainly chemicals, pharmaceuticals and medical equipment.

Stojiljkovic insisted Yugoslavia was "attractive for its stable economy and the size of its market... We intend to maintain economic stability in 1997 and to strongly pursue privatisation and restructuring of overall economy," he said.

Bilateral trade is expected to exceed $70 million this year, close to the 1989 level, Mladen Obradovic, consultant with the Serbian Chamber of Commerce told Reuters. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
